# PRD 006: seat types

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 006-seat-types.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

| --- | --- |

| status | draft |
| updated | 2026-11-25 |
| owner | pm-001 |
| summary | Every community role names one of ten types that says how its seat lives: what it is for, when it is compacted or closed, and what it must keep written down. Types are pij's fixed set; roles stay the open set each repo builds on top of them. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

A pij community is meant to be a team of experts that learns a problem space nobody could map in advance, not only a way to run coders in parallel. Today pij cannot tell those seats apart. The daemon acts on four seat roles (`prime`, `pm`, `worker`, `pa`), and assigning any other community role stamps the seat `worker`, so a topic expert, a graph keeper and a coder look the same. A role's `kind` (`specialist` or `general`) carries no rules, and nearly every role is `specialist`. On 2026-11-24 the primes of five fleets were asked how they use their seats. All five asked for a named knowledge type, and they sorted their seats into the same few kinds without having words for them. The operator's rulings from that conversation: a coder or reviewer is compacted after every job because its size matters more than what it remembers; a knowledge seat is the expert, not the database, and is responsible for writing what it learns into graphs or markdown that can be read without it.

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-operator | operator | Know what kind of seat each one is and trust that it is treated accordingly. |
| a-prime | prime | Create a role by saying how it should live, without writing its lifecycle rules by hand each time. |
| a-holder | role holder | Be told, at the start, what kind of seat it is and what that requires of it. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | pij can tell a coder from an expert from a human's window, for every seat that holds a role. |
| g-2 | A repo builds any role it needs on a type, and never needs to change pij to do it. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | Having the daemon enforce a type's rules, such as compacting a coder itself. This PRD states the rules and tells the seat; enforcement is later work. |
| n-2 | Changing the large-seat alert, the idle nudge or which fleet messages may wake a seat. |
| n-3 | Changing what a prime, a project manager or a PA is allowed to do, or any other permission rule (PRD 003). The `--role pm\|worker\|pa` flag on spawn and link keeps working; `worker` simply means no authority of its own. |
| n-4 | Letting a repo define its own type. |

| req-01 | Every role has one type | A role names exactly one type from pij's set: `prime`, `pa`, `project-manager`, `coder`, `reviewer`, `worker`, `knowledge`, `steward`, `watcher` or `human-window`. `pij directory add` and `edit` take `--type`, and `add` refuses a role with no type, listing the ten with one line each. | prime | must | [ ] planned | `pij directory add x --why y` with no type or template refuses and prints the ten types; the same call with `--type knowledge` writes a role whose document shows that type. | operator rulings, design conversation 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25 | — | — |
| req-02 | Each type says what it means | pij ships one short definition per type: what the seat is for, when it is compacted or closed, and what it must keep. A coder builds one step and is compacted after every job. A reviewer judges one piece of work at its exact version, independently of its author, and is compacted after every job unless its role keeps standing context, as security may. A worker does one other piece of work and is closed. A knowledge seat is the expert who owns one area and keeps what it learns written down. A steward is the only writer of one shared thing. A project manager runs a workstream and holds its history. A watcher reacts to events and rebuilds from current state. A human-window is one person's seat into the fleet. Prime and PA keep the duties they have today. | role holder | must | [ ] planned | For each of the ten types, pij prints its definition on request, and a seat started in a role of that type receives it. | operator rulings 2026-11-25; interviews with five primes 2026-11-24 | — | — |
| req-03 | A type asks for what it needs | Creating a role asks for what its type requires. A knowledge role names the artefact it keeps current (a graph or a file path). A steward role names the one thing it is sole writer of. `add` refuses when the required field is missing and names it. | prime | must | [ ] planned | `pij directory add x --type knowledge --why y` with no artefact refuses and names the missing field; with one, the role document records it. | operator ruling 2026-11-25: knowledge seats project what they know into static forms | — | — |
| req-04 | A seat holds roles of one type | The prime's view marks a seat that holds roles of two different types and proposes the split, since their rules conflict (a coder is compacted after each job; an expert is kept). | prime | should | [ ] planned | With one seat assigned a coder role and a knowledge role, `pij directory` lists it as an action naming both roles. | PRD 001 req-29 boundary review; operator, 2026-11-25 | — | — |
| req-05 | One label per seat, and three types carry authority | A seat has one label, its type, shown by `pij directory` and `pij list`. Only three types carry authority of their own: prime, project manager and PA keep exactly the powers those seats have today. The other seven carry none, which is what `worker` means today, so there is no separate worker label to keep in step. Who may govern a particular seat still comes from its recorded parent and the prime designation. | operator | must | [ ] planned | A seat assigned a knowledge role and a seat assigned a coder role show different types in `pij list --json` and neither has any power a plain worker lacks; a prime, a project manager and a PA can do everything they could before; and every existing permission test still passes. | operator ruling 2026-11-25: just prime, pm and pa, simplify; code reading: every other role is stamped worker at assignment | — | — |
| req-06 | Roles extend types; types are fixed | A role inherits its type's rules and may add its own. A type marks each of its rules as fixed or as a default a role may change with a reason: a coder is always compacted after every job, while a reviewer role may keep standing context instead. A repo cannot add a type. When no type fits, the creator picks the nearest, puts the difference in the role's rules and records a type suggestion that the pij project can read. | prime | should | [ ] planned | A coder role edited to remove the compact-after-each-job rule is refused; a reviewer role created to keep standing context is accepted and its document records the reason; a recorded type suggestion appears in the view. | operator, 2026-11-25: dynamic roles come off one of our base types; security is a reviewer whose compaction is optional | — | — |
| req-07 | Existing roles get a type | One command gives every existing role a type, proposing one from the role's template and id and leaving the rest for the prime to choose. `kind` and `lifecycle` are retired, and a role document written before the change still reads. | prime | must | [ ] planned | Run on a community of roles written before this change, the command leaves no role without a type, lists each one it could not decide, and `pij directory` reads the result. | role documents in five projects use kind and lifecycle today | — | — |
| req-08 | Every type ships a seed template a repo can change | pij ships a seed template for each of the ten types: the text a seat of that type is told at start. The prime and project-manager seeds carry firm guidance on how to govern. The coder, reviewer, security and other seeds are working examples that a repo is encouraged to replace or extend for its own work. A repo edits its own copy of any of them, and a prime may change its own. | prime | must | [ ] planned | pij prints a seed for each of the ten types; a repo's edited copy of the coder seed is what a new coder there receives; and a prime's edit to the prime seed is accepted and recorded with its reason. | operator, 2026-11-25: seed templates for all of these; primes are encouraged to change them and can change their own | — | — |
